_comment: Curated source of truth for the flash sheet. Edit by hand.
Run `node tools/ink.mjs --refresh` to pull the `github` block for any
entry with a `repo`, then inline everything into index.html.
cell: no longer a position — the sheet has no grid. It is a running
ORDER: lowest first. It sets which piece is numbered i, and the
earlier a piece comes the sooner the packer picks its spot. Any
number is valid; missing sorts last.
motif: 'auto' reads the piece's own words and picks the form that means
the right thing; or pin one by name (see MOTIFS in index.html).
url: optional. Omit it for private work — the piece renders, but there is
nothing to claim, which is on-theme rather than a gap.
repo: optional, and it IS published — ink.mjs inlines it into index.html.
Leave it off a private repo you would rather not name, and set the
`github` block by hand; --refresh then leaves that entry alone.
What the reader shows when you open a piece:
problem: what it is for, in plain words. One or two sentences.
build:   the rough architecture, three to five short lines. An abstract,
not a file listing — how the thing is put together.
terms:   'open' | 'profit' | 'private'. A flash sheet quotes a price for
every piece on it; this is that line.

pieces.title: smart blinds
pieces.banner: Blinds that read the light and decide for themselves.
pieces.problem: The blinds shipped with an official app that drops its connection and loses track of which blind is which. This is the same hardware driven from a web page instead: scan, connect, send any blind to any position, and have it remember them next time.
build: a static page — no framework, no build step, no dependencies
Web Bluetooth straight from the browser to the blind
speaks the MotionBlinds BLE protocol, falls back to Tuiss's own
AES-128 ECB hand-rolled in about a hundred lines
service worker precaches the lot, so it works offline

pieces.title: fontloop
pieces.banner: A brief in plain English; a real typeface out.
pieces.problem: Drawing a display face means committing a few hundred curves by hand before you find out whether the idea was any good. This turns a written brief into a style descriptor and renders the whole family from it, so an idea can be judged in seconds instead of weeks — and then compiled to a font you can actually install.
build: the brief goes to a model, which returns a style descriptor
a parametric engine draws from it — tagged skeleton strokes, modulated pen
pen angle gives the real Didone thick/thin; authored end caps give the serifs
profile-based sidebearings space it; heavy weights auto-open their counters
every descriptor compiles to an installable .otf, re-parsed to validate

pieces.title: avatars
pieces.banner: One file defines a character; everything else is generated.
pieces.problem: An end-to-end test of how much of a consistent synthetic identity can be automated. A single definition holds a character's look, voice and world, and everything downstream — the images, the writing, the posting schedule — is derived from that one file rather than authored per post.
build: one persona definition is the single source of truth for look, voice and scene
a diffusion model draws the images, an LLM writes the copy, both prompted from it
a reference library holds the face steady across generations
Postgres keeps the history, so it never repeats itself back at you
runs on scheduled CI — no server, and it can be driven from a phone
